implemented_requirements.requirement: Player controls snake using directional inputs
implemented_requirements.evidence: KEY_DIRS maps arrow keys and WASD to direction vectors; on_key() updates self.next_dir when state == "play" (lines defining KEY_DIRS and the on_key method).

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake moves around board and eats food items
implemented_requirements.evidence: tick() computes new head position (nx, ny), checks for food with "if (nx, ny) == self.food", increments score and spawns new food.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Snake grows in length each time it eats
implemented_requirements.evidence: When food is eaten, tick() does not pop the tail (self.snake.pop()) so the snake list length increases.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Game ends if the snake collides with itself or the boundary
implemented_requirements.evidence: tick() checks "if not (0 <= nx < COLS and 0 <= ny < ROWS) or (nx, ny) in self.snake" and calls game_over().
draw_board() is called at the end of tick() and redraws the snake and food on the canvas.

implemented_requirements.requirement: Show the current score based on food eaten
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.status.config(text="Score: %d   Difficulty: %s" % (self.score, self.name)) updates the score after each tick and also on game over.
DIFFS dictionary defines Easy/Medium/Hard with different intervals; show_menu() displays options and start() uses the selected interval.

judge.summary: The provided Python/Tkinter program implements a fully functional classic Snake game. All core requirements—directional control, movement, food consumption, growth, collision detection, board refresh, score display, and selectable difficulty levels—are present in the source code. The code appears syntactically correct and ready to run in an environment with Tkinter support, leading to a passing verdict.
